task.description: Idiom/scope/decision-record hard gate on the ISS-0414 service_catalog safety-net implementation: (1) idiom check of sweep_service_catalog_orphans/1 against the module's existing style; (2) design fidelity (reuses existing guard, no age threshold, unconditional delete with warn-log, wired at the same two test_helper.exs boundary points); (3) adequacy of the 5 tests in service_catalog_reaper_test.exs; (4) decision-record consistency; (5) legitimacy of the design's 2 deferred open questions; (6) regression run.
acceptance_criteria: Idiom, supervision, scope-creep, and decision-record checks performed against the real diff, not the design doc alone
5 tests read and confirmed non-vacuous, covering the design's specified scenarios
PASS only if no genuine defect found; otherwise FAILED routed back to ELIXIR-DEV

result.summary:
1. Idiom check: read the new sweep_service_catalog_orphans/1 (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex lines 206-274) against sweep_orphans/2's existing style (lines 131-204) side by side. Naming (sweep_*_orphans, own_tag, rows), the try/rescue/after skeleton, Sandbox.mode(repo, :auto) then :manual restore in `after`, `Logger.info` for deferral / `Logger.warning` for an anomalous nonzero find / `Logger.error` with Exception.format(:error, exception, __STACKTRACE__) for the rescue branch, and read-before-delete (SELECT then DELETE, never a bare bulk DELETE) all match sweep_orphans/2's own idiom exactly. No case-do hand-rolled state machine, no new process, no GenServer -- this is a plain function extending an existing test-support module, which is the right shape for a suite-boundary hook (not a candidate for gen_statem at all -- there is no state to manage across calls). Idiomatic, consistent with the file it extends.

2. Design fidelity: confirmed line-for-line against design doc SS2.4/SS2.5/SS3. own_tag + concurrent_invocation_present?/2 reused verbatim, zero duplication (git diff confirms these private helpers have zero hunks touching them). No min_age_seconds-equivalent parameter -- correctly omitted per SS2.1's argument (service_catalog rows are never held open across a test's duration, so no age buffer is needed; verified this claim against service_catalog_test.exs/admin_services_test.exs/service_scope_validator_test.exs, none of which hold a row open past their own on_exit/1). Delete is unconditional (`DELETE FROM service_catalog` with no WHERE clause), matching SS2.4 step 6 exactly, with the required :warning log naming every found service_id/scope pair first. test/test_helper.exs wiring: two new lines, one before ExUnit.start() immediately after the existing sweep_orphans() call, one inside the same ExUnit.after_suite/1 callback immediately after the existing sweep_orphans() call inside it -- exactly the 'two plain adjacent calls, no new wrapper function' placement SS3 specifies, not folded into a shared wrapper.

3. Test coverage (test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs, 5 describe blocks): (a) empty-table test actually pre-sweeps then asserts {:ok, %{deleted: 0}} and Repo.aggregate(Entry, :count) == 0 -- non-vacuous, checks real DB state, not just the return tuple. (b) mixed scope test inserts one :global and one :tenant-scoped row (with a real tenant FK via insert_tenant!), asserts both existed before and both are gone after, deleted >= 2 -- exercises the 'no scope-based filtering' claim for real. (c) concurrent-invocation-deferral test opens a genuine second Postgrex connection tagged with a fake application_name with no matching TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP suffix, confirms via a direct pg_stat_activity query that the tag is visible before asserting {:deferred, :concurrent_invocation} and that the pre-inserted row survives untouched, then closes that connection and re-sweeps to confirm the row is deleted once the hazard clears -- this is a real concurrency scenario, not a mock. (d) sibling test_parallel.sh test computes the invocation's own group suffix from a real `SHOW application_name` and branches its own assertion (expect_proceed?) on whether this invocation is itself running under a group tag today -- correctly falls back to exercising the plain ISS-0110 'no group tag, still excluded correctly' path when run standalone, rather than silently no-op'ing; this is a deliberate, honest adaptation for the two different real-invocation shapes, not weakened coverage. (e) failure-mode test uses a BrokenRepo whose query!/1-2 always raises but whose get_dynamic_repo/0 delegates to the real Letflow.Repo (so Sandbox.mode/2 still resolves) -- isolates the forced failure to exactly the SELECT/DELETE path per the design's own rationale, and the security reviewer's independently-run test output already confirms the real rescue-branch log line fires. All 5 are non-vacuous and match the design's SS4 required coverage list one-for-one.

4. Decision-record consistency: grepped docs/anti-patterns.md and docs/migration/decisions/ for service_catalog/TenantSchemaReaper -- zero hits in either. No existing decision record is touched or contradicted. service_catalog's deliberate global-table design (lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex) is unchanged -- this diff adds zero lib/letflow/ files (git diff --stat confirms only test/support/, test/test_helper.exs, docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md, and the design doc itself changed).

5. Open questions: OQ-1 (mid-run leak healing) is a structural limitation of any suite-boundary sweep, correctly left open with a stated future trigger (a third incident), consistent with iss064's own precedent for the same gap on tenant_schemas -- not silently resolved. OQ-2 (renaming TenantSchemaReaper) was explicitly left for REVIEWER to weigh in on: having read the actual moduledoc, the two-responsibility shape is not a code smell yet -- both sweeps share the exact same concurrency-guard mechanism and boundary-call-site convention, the moduledoc clearly separates the two responsibilities into their own labeled sections (ISS-0110/ISS-0217 vs ISS-0414), and each has its own independently-attributable test file. A rename now would touch every historical doc reference (ISS-0064/0110/0217 records) for zero behavioral gain -- agreeing with the design's own rejection. Recommend leaving OQ-2 open rather than acting on it now; revisit only if a third table's reaper need arrives and the module accretes a third unrelated responsibility. OQ-3 (no min_age_seconds for service_catalog) is legitimately narrower-by-design per point 2 above, not an oversight.

No scope creep found: no new abstraction, behaviour, or macro introduced; the change is exactly sized to the stated problem (one new function on an existing module, two call-site lines, one new test file), matching the design's own stated change class.

No type-safety gap worth filing: the new function's return type ({:ok, %{deleted: n}} | {:deferred, :concurrent_invocation}) is a plain, already-fully-enumerable tagged tuple with a @spec: there is no invalid-state class here that a struct/Ecto.Enum change would make unrepresentable -- it mirrors sweep_orphans/2's own already-reviewed shape.

6. Regression: ran `mix test test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs test/letflow/routers/admin_services_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator_test.exs` myself -- Result: 74 passed, 0 failures. Also ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean, no output) and `mix format --check-formatted` (clean, no output).

No defect found. PASS.
result.routing: PASS -- no genuine defect found.
